rare_plays.name: Rare Play Trigger
resolution: Find the pitcher result as normal from the 2d6 on the pitcher's card.
Re-roll the percentile dice.

Check the chart matching the base state (bases empty vs runners on base) and the pitcher result (BALLPARK or WHEELHOUSE, PATIENT incl. PATIENT-OUT and /PATIENT/, TOUGH incl. TOUGH-OUT, IN-PLAY incl. /IN-PLAY/, DEFENSE incl. RANGE or ERROR).
Apply the entry for the re-rolled percentile range.
rare_plays.trigger: The initial roll of the percentile dice (or FAC % result) is 00.

chart.result: Pitcher calls out trainer and manager due to discomfort. Pitcher must be removed from game. Check for injury.
Catcher is hit by a foul ball and momentarily incapacitated. Check for injury. If no injury, catcher shakes it off and stays in game.
Batter smashes a line drive off pitcher. Catcher retrieves ball and throws out batter with RUN rating of 6 or less. 7 or more is safe with a SINGLE. Check pitcher for injury.
Batter grounds out to SS and injures leg running to 1st base. Batter must be removed from game. Check batter for injury.

Weather takes a turn and game is delayed by rain (stadium with a roof suffers power outage). Roll 1d6. If result is 1 or 2, no affect on game; if result is 3-4, there is a lengthy delay and both pitchers must be replaced; if 5 to 6, game is postponed (record as official game if 6th inning or later).

Batter hits a line drive to right field. The right fielder misplays the ball and it sails over his head. Batter with a RUN rating of 5 or less stays at 1st base for a long SINGLE. Batter with a RUN of 6 or more reaches 2nd base for a DOUBLE and heads for 3rd base. The relay throw from the SS is on time and the batter is thrown out at 3rd base.

Batter hits a deep drive, the CF leaps at the wall... if the fielder has an A Range, he snares the ball robbing the batter of a HR. Otherwise, a fan reaches out and takes the ball away from the fielder. After several minutes of deliberation, the umpires rule the play a HR for the batter.
Batter grounds sharply down the right field line. Thinking the ball was foul, the batter does not run to 1st base. The ump rules the ball fair and the batter is thrown out by the RF.

Batter hits a sinking liner to left field. The LF makes a diving play on the ball and the ump calls the batter out! The manager bounds out of the dug out to protest the call. The umps get together to discuss the play. If the LF has an A range, the call stands and the batter is out. Otherwise, the umps reverse the call and the batter is credited with a SINGLE and safe at 1st base, runners advance 1 base.

Batter hits a towering ball into the outfield where it hits a bird. Both the bird and ball fall into fair territory and the batter is safe at 2nd base with a DOUBLE. If the stadium has a roof, the ball lodges into a speaker or roof support and the umps award a ground rule DOUBLE for the batter.
Batter singles to RF, but makes a wide turn and RF makes a great throw to 1B. The batter is caught in a rundown and eventually tagged out by the 2B (score the put out 9-3-6-4).
Batter lines the ball down the third base line where it caroms off the wall in foul territory to the LF. Thinking the ball foul, the batter does not run and is thrown out 7-4-3 by the alert LF.

rare_plays.name: Rare Plays: Bases Empty, BALLPARK or WHEELHOUSE
resolution: Apply the entry below for the re-rolled percentile range.
rare_plays.trigger: Initial percentile 00, pitcher result BALLPARK or WHEELHOUSE, bases empty. Re-roll percentile.

chart.result: Pitcher's velocity is noticeably down. Manager checks on him and pitcher must be removed from game. Check for injury.
Ump calls borderline pitch a ball; batter walks (BB). Catcher barks at umpire and umpire immediately ejects the catcher.
Pitcher just misses on a 3-0 count and walks batter (BB). Pitcher has a few choice words for the umpire and umpire ejects the pitcher.
Ump calls borderline pitch a strike and rings up the batter (SO). Batter argues call and is ejected.
Batter HBP. If another batter is HBP this game, both benches are warned. Any subsequent HBP result in pitcher being ejected from the game.
Batter HBP and charges mound, both teams spill on to the field with a lot of pushing and shoving. Next HBP this game ignites a brawl with batter and pitcher being ejected and suspended 5 games each.
Umpire misses obvious strike; batter walks (BB). Pitcher is rattled, all PATIENT results for this pitcher the remainder of the inning are automatic BB.
Ump loses track of pitch count and calls ball 4, ball 3. Re-roll all four dice and restart the current at-bat.

Pitcher walks batter (BB). If pitcher's WP range ends in 32 or higher, ball sails over everyone's head. A batter with a RUN rating of 7 or higher advances to 3rd base on the wild pitch; other batters only advance to 2nd base. Pitchers with a WP range that ends in 31 or less just miss the zone, no wild pitch.

Batter is HBP; check batter for injury. Batting team retaliates by hitting the first batter of the pitching team next half inning. Umpires warn both benches. Any further HBP this game results in pitcher being ejected.

rare_plays.name: Rare Plays: Bases Empty, PATIENT
resolution: Apply the entry below for the re-rolled percentile range.
rare_plays.trigger: Initial percentile 00, pitcher result PATIENT (or PATIENT-OUT or /PATIENT/), bases empty. Re-roll percentile.

chart.result: Batter appears to injure himself while trying to check his swing at a borderline pitch and strikes out (SO). Check batter for injury.
Ump calls borderline pitch a strike; batter strikes out (SO). Batter questions call and umpire overreacts and ejects batter!

IF 7th inning or later, strike zone has become increasingly larger each inning. All TOUGH results for both teams are automatic strike outs (SO) for remainder of game. If 6th inning or earlier, all TOUGH results for this pitcher are automatic strike outs (SO) for the remainder of the inning only.

Ump calls obvious strike a ball (BB). Several coaches on pitching team complain about call. Ump does not eject anyone, but squeezes the strike zone even more. Change all TOUGH results to PATIENT for the remainder of the inning while the current pitcher is in the game.

Batter swings at wild pitch that gets past catcher. Record strike out (SO) and check if batter is safe or out by rolling 2d6. If the dice result is equal or less than the batter's RUN rating, batter beats throw to 1st base. Batting team gets an 'extra' out (i.e., need 4 outs to end batting team's inning). If the dice result is greater than the RUN rating, catcher throws batter out at 1st base to complete the strike out (SO).

Batter strikes out (SO) on great pitch by pitcher, but catcher drops the ball. Roll 1d6. If equal or less than the catcher's E rating, catcher makes easy throw to 1B to secure the strike out. If the d6 result is higher than the catcher's E rating, catcher throws wildly allowing batter to safely reach base. Batter with a RUN rating of 7 or more advances to 2nd base on error; otherwise batter safe at 1st base. Record as SO and E2. Batting team gets an extra out (need 4 outs to complete the inning).

Umpire has large strike zone this game. Change all PATIENT results to TOUGH for the current pitchers (both teams) for the remainder of the game. This change does not apply to any new relief pitchers that may enter the game; only applies to the pitchers currently in the game.

Foul tip hits catcher in a tender spot. Check catcher for injury. If catcher remains in game, remaining batters this inning roll on their TOUGH sections until the half inning ends or there is a pitching change. If catcher is removed due to injury, remaining batters this inning roll on their WHEELHOUSE sections until the half inning ends or there is a pitching change.

rare_plays.name: Rare Plays: Bases Empty, TOUGH
resolution: Apply the entry below for the re-rolled percentile range.
rare_plays.trigger: Initial percentile 00, pitcher result TOUGH (or TOUGH-OUT), bases empty. Re-roll percentile.

chart.result: Batter grounds out to SS (G6) and appears to injure himself running to 1st base. Batter removed from game and check for injury.
Batter lines ball off pitcher's leg. Batter is safe at 1st base with a single. Check pitcher for injury.

Rain causes a delay. If 5th inning later, roll 1d10 after every half inning, if result is equal or less then the inning number, umpires call the game due to heavy rain. Game is considered official. If dome stadium or 4th inning or less, there is a slight delay, but game continues. Use BALLPARK to resolve this at-bat. If the result is WHEELHOUSE, next batter automatically checks his WHEELHOUSE section. If IN-PLAY, remaining batters this inning use TOUGH.

Re-roll the 2d6 and check the pitcher's card as normal. All remaining batters this inning automatically check that result until the pitcher is replaced or the inning ends. If the game is in the 1st or 2nd innings, the batter hits a long fly ball foul. Re-roll all four dice and restart this at-bat.

Batter hits a slow roller near the third base line. If the visiting team is batting, the pitcher makes a terrific bare-handed play to throw out the batter at 1st base. If the home team is batting, the pitcher is unable to pick up the ball cleanly and the batter is safe on 1st with an infield single.

Roll 1d6. If the result is 1, 2 or 3, the batter hits a ground ball up the middle that trickles through the infield for a single. If the result is 4 or 5, the next batter also hits a ground ball up the middle for a single, runner advances 1 base. If the result is 6, batter singles and next batter hits into a 1-6-3 double play.

Batter hits slow roller to 1B who fields the ball and throws to Pitcher covering the base. The batter and pitcher collide knocking both players to the ground. Roll 1d6, if the result is equal or less than the pitcher's E rating, the batter is called out; otherwise he is safe on an infield single. Check both players for injury.

If the stadium is a dome or has a roof, the power suddenly goes out. If an open air stadium, a violent storm pops up. In either event, the game is delayed. Roll 2d6 and multiple the result by 10 to determine how long the delay lasts. If the delay is 50 minutes or more (5 or more on the dice), both pitchers stiffen up and must be replaced. If the result is 40 minutes or less (2 to 4 on the dice), reduce the pitcher's fatigue rating by 2 and continue game.

Batter hits a hard ground down the line (3B if right-handed batter, 1B if left-handed batter). Ball bounces off the base and into foul territory. Fielder assumes the ball is foul and does not immediately attempt to retrieve it. Umpire calls ball fair. Batter safe at 1st with single and batter's with a RUN rating of 7 or higher coast into 2nd base with a double. If the ball was hit down the 1B line and the batter has a RUN rating of 8 or more, he has the option to try to advance to 3rd base for a triple using the coach's choice attempt an extra base chart.
Batter hits pop-up into short CF. CF and infielder collide (roll 1d6, 1 to 3 = SS, 4 to 6 = 2B). Batter safe at 1st base with a single. Check both fielders for injury.
Batter hits a bloop single into CF and trips rounding 1st base. The CF tosses the ball to the SS who relays it to the 1B who tags the embarrassed runner out for a 8-6-3 put out.

rare_plays.name: Rare Plays: Bases Empty, IN-PLAY
resolution: Apply the entry below for the re-rolled percentile range.
rare_plays.trigger: Initial percentile 00, pitcher result IN-PLAY (or /IN-PLAY/), bases empty. Re-roll percentile.

chart.result: Ball is smashed down the 3rd base line. 3B with an A or B range stops the ball holding the batter to a single. 3B with a range of C or worse cannot get to the ball and it bounces into the corner for a double. Check 3B for injury.
Batter hits a slow roller to 1B and the players collide at 1st base. 1B holds on to the ball for the out. Check both players for injury

Hard ground ball in hole between 2nd and 1st base. 2B with an A range makes unbelievable diving stop and throws out batter at 1st base. 2B with a B range knocks down the ball, but can't make the play. Batter safe at 1st with a single. 2B with a C or worse misses ball and it rolls all the way to the wall. Batter safe at 2nd base with a double.

Batter hit routine ground ball to 2B. Roll 1d6, if result is equal or less than E rating, 2B bobbles ball, but recovers in time to throw out batter at 1st base. If the result is greater than 2B's E rating, fielder bobbles ball and throws wildly. Batter safe at 2nd base on the 2-base error.

2B leaps for line drive over his head. If the 2B has an A or B range rating, roll 1d6. 1 to 3 he makes the sensational catch, 4 to 6 the ball is just over his glove. Players with a C or worse also cannot reach the ball giving the batter a single to RF. In all cases, the 2B lands awkwardly. Check for injury.

Batter hits a sinking line drive to LF who makes a diving attempt. Check LF for injury. If fielder is not injured, he retrieves ball in time to hold the batter to a double. If the fielder is injured, the batter makes it all the way around the bases for an inside the park HR.

Batter lines a single to LF. Roll 1d6. If the result is higher than LF's E rating, he badly misplays the ball allowing the batter to reach 3rd base on the single and 2 base error. If the result is equal or lower than the E rating, LF bobbles ball, but is able to throw out batter at 2nd base. Batter is credited with a single and is out 7-4 attempting to stretch the hit into a double.

SS makes diving stop on ground ball in the hole. Roll 1d6. If the result is higher than the SS's E rating, the throw to 1st base is wild and into the dugout. Batter safe on 2nd on 2-base error. If the result is equal or less than the E rating, the throw just beats the batter for the out.

SS leaps for line drive over his head. If the SS has an A or B range rating, roll 1d6. 1 to 3 he makes the sensational catch, 4 to 6 the ball is just over his glove. Players with a C or worse also cannot reach the ball giving the batter a single to LF. In all cases, the SS lands awkwardly. Check for injury.

SS ranges up the middle for a ground ball through the pitcher. SS with an A range easily fields the ball and throws out batter. For all other SS, roll 1d6. If the SS has a B or C range and the d6 is 1 to 3, the SS makes the play and throws out the batter. If the SS is a D or F and the d6 is 1 to 2, the SS makes the player and throws out the batter. Otherwise, the SS just misses the ball. Batter is safe on first with a single to CF.

Slow roller hit down 3rd base line. 3B with A range picks the ball and throws a bullet to 1st base for the out. All other 3B, roll 1d6. If the result is 1 to 3, batter is out. If the result is 4 to 6, batter beats throw for an infield single.

3B ranges for a foul ball and falls over the railing into a camera well. Roll 1d6, if result is 1 to 3, 3B makes the catch for the out. If the result is 4 to 6, 3B is unable to catch the foul ball (restart the at-bat for this batter). In either case, check the 3B for injury.

Hard liner to 3B is dropped. Roll 1d6. If result is equal to or less than the E rating, 3B recovers and throws out batter at 1st. If result is higher than the E rating, 3B picks up ball, but makes a poor throw that pulls the 1B off the bag. Official scorer gives 3B a 1-base error.

Batter hits a rocket to deep center field. CF with A or B range catches the ball before slamming into the wall. He holds on for the out. CF with C or worse range is unable to catch up to ball and it takes a big bounce off the wall. Batter safe at 3rd base with a triple and may attempt an inside the park HR using the Coach's Choice / Attempt Extra Base Chart and the RF ARM.

CF crashes head first into wall chasing fly ball. Roll 1d6. If the result is equal or less than the E rating, CF holds on for the out. Otherwise, CF drops the ball. Official scorer scores a double for the batter. In either event, check CF for injury.

CF picks up single up the middle and fires to 1st base to try to get the batter as he returns to the base. Roll 1d6. If the result is equal or lower than the E rating, the throw is on target, but late and the batter is safe. If the result is higher than the E rating the throw is off target and into the dugout allowing the batter to advance to 2nd base on the throwing error.
RF pulls up while going for a pop fly down the line. The ball lands on the line and is ruled a fair ball and the batter coasts into 2nd base with a double. Check RF for injury.

Routine fly ball to RF. Roll 1d6. If the result is higher than the E rating, the RF drops the ball and the batter is safe at 1st base on the error. If the result is equal or lower than the E rating, the RF bobbles the ball, but secures the catch for the out.

Pop up in front of home plate is dropped by catcher. Roll 1d10 if the result is equal or lower than the RUN rating, batter beats the throw to 1st base. Otherwise, catcher recovers and throws out batter. In either event, charge catcher with an error.

Batter tops the ball in front of the plate. Catcher bounces up and fields the ball. Roll 1d6. If the result is equal or lower than the E rating, the catcher makes a good throw to 1st base for the out. If the result is higher than the E rating, the throw sails down the RF line and the batter is safe on 2nd base on the throwing error.
High foul ball is dropped by the catcher. Official scorer gives catcher an error. Restart the at-bat for this batter.
3B drops easy foul ball. Official scorer gives 3B an error. Restart the at-bat for this batter.
1B trips over bag running after foul ball. Check 1B for injury. Restart the at-bat for this batter.

rare_plays.name: Rare Plays: Bases Empty, DEFENSE
resolution: Apply the entry below for the re-rolled percentile range.
rare_plays.trigger: Initial percentile 00, pitcher result DEFENSE (or RANGE or ERROR), bases empty. Re-roll percentile.

chart.result: Batter hits a drive down the left field line. The ball bounces around in the corner before LF is able to retrieve it. Batter with a RUN rating of 5 or less is safe on 2nd base with a double, all runners score. Batter with a RUN rating of 6 or more, is thrown out at 3rd base trying for the triple if the LF ARM is equal or less than 7. Otherwise, batter is safe with a triple, all runners score.

Batter hits a drive down the right field line. The ball bounces around in the corner before RF is able to retrieve it. Batter with a RUN rating of 4 or less is safe on 1st base with a single, all runners score. Batter with a RUN rating of 5 or more, is thrown out at 2nd base trying for the double if the RF ARM is equal or less than 6. Otherwise, batter is safe with a double, all runners score.

Batter hits a drive down to deep center field that bounces wildly off the wall. The CF eventually retrieves the ball and throws it to 3rd base. Batter with a RUN rating of 6 or less is safe on 2nd base with a double, all runners score. Batter with a RUN rating of 7 or more, is thrown out at 3rd base trying for the triple if the CF ARM is equal or less than 7. Otherwise, batter is safe with a triple, all runners score.

CF reaches down for a sinking line drive and grabs it on a short hop. The umpire rules a catch and the CF doubles off the lead runner. The batting team's manager protests. If the CF is a D or F range, the umpires reverse the call and award the batter a single and runners advance 1 base. Otherwise, the call stands as called, double play, other runners hold.

Weather takes a turn and game is delayed by rain (stadium with a roof suffers power outage). Roll 1d6. If result is 1 or 2, no affect on game; if result is 3-4, there is a lengthy delay and both pitchers must be replaced; if 5 to 6, roll 1d6 after each inning. If the result is 6, the game is postponed (record as official game if 6th inning or later).

RF makes terrific running catch. If RF ARM rating is equal or less than 6, the RF throws out the lead runner trying to advance. If the ARM rating is higher than the RUN rating, the runner advances to the next base or scores. In all cases, other runners advance 1 base.

CF makes diving catch and immediately pops back up. If CF ARM rating is equal or less than 6, the CF throws out the lead runner trying to advance; other runners advance 1 base. If the ARM rating is higher than the RUN rating, the runner decides not to test the CF's arm and all runners hold.

LF makes a sliding catch. If ARM rating is equal or less than 7, the lead runner is unable to return to the best and doubled off. In all other cases, the runners return safely and hold at their current base.

If Pitcher has not allowed a run in this game, change all future BALLPARK and WHEELHOUSE results to TOUGH. If the pitcher has allowed 1 or more runs, change all future TOUGH results to BALLPARK while he remains in this game. Re-roll on the batter's WHEELHOUSE section to resolve this at-bat.

Batter scorches the ball down the RF line. If visiting team is batting, ump rules the ball foul. If home team is batting, the ball stays fair, but bounces into foul territory where a fan reaches out and grabs the ball thinking it is foul. Umps rule fan interference and award a ground rule double, runners advance 2 bases.
Batter hits a high fly ball that gets lost in the sun / lights. The ball bounces harmlessly in the short outfield. Batter is safe at 1st with a single and all runners advance 2 bases.

OF makes running catch on deep fly ball and crashes into the wall. He hangs onto the ball for the out, but is dazed. All runners advance 2 bases. Check OF for injury. To determine the OF, roll 1d6. 1-2 = LF, 3-4 = CF, 5-6 = RF.
1B makes running catch of foul ball. Roll 1d10. If the lead runner's RUN rating is less than the d10 result, all runners advance 1 base. Otherwise, all runners hold.

3B ranges into foul territory for a foul ball, but it bounces off his glove. SS with a range of A or B is able to catch the ball before it hits the ground. All other SS are unable to get to the ball. All runners hold.

rare_plays.name: Rare Plays: Runners On, BALLPARK or WHEELHOUSE
resolution: Apply the entry below for the re-rolled percentile range.
rare_plays.trigger: Initial percentile 00, pitcher result BALLPARK or WHEELHOUSE, runners on base. Re-roll percentile.

chart.result: Pitcher walks batter and calls time. Training and manager visit mound and pitcher must be removed from game with an injury. He misses the next 4 games.

Fast ball gets away from pitcher and drills batter in the ribs. Hit By Pitch (HBP). Batter walks to 1st base, but is in obvious discomfort. Trainer removes player from the game. Roll 1d6. Batter misses that many games before he is able to return.

Catcher with an A range blocks pitch in the dirt. If his ARM is 1, 2 or 3 he fires to the lead base and the runner is tagged out. Catcher with a 4 or 5 ARM does not make the throw. Restart the at-bat. Catcher with a B or worse range misses the pitch and runners advance 1 base on the passed ball (PB).

Pitcher uncorks a breaking pitch that bounces before the plate and gets by the catcher for a wild pitch. Runners advance 1 base. If the pitcher's WP range ends in 33 or higher, the next pitch is also a wild pitch and runners advance 1 base. Batter eventually walks (BB).

Catcher with a C, D or F range gets crossed up and misses the pitch. Runners advance 1 base on passed ball (PB). An A or B catcher knocks the ball down and holds the runners. Re-roll the percentile dice and check the batter's PATIENT section to resolve the at-bat.

Catcher with a D or F range gets crossed up and misses the pitch. Runners advance 1 base on passed ball (PB). An A, B or C catcher catches the ball down and holds the runners. Re-roll the percentile dice and check the batter's PATIENT section to resolve the at-bat.

Pitcher with a WP range that ends in 31 or higher sails the ball past the catcher. All runners advance 1 base. A lead runner with a RUN rating of 8 or higher advances 2 bases. Other pitchers (no WP or WP of 30), no wild pitch. Batter takes the count full and walks (BB).

Catcher is unable to hang onto the pitch and it rolls to the backstop. All runners advance 1 base. If catcher has an ARM of 1, he throws to the lead base and runner is out returning to the base after rounding it. Other catchers throw wildly allowing runners to advance an extra base. Batter walks (BB).

Catcher expects a different pitch and the ball gets by him for a passed ball (PB), all runners advance 1 base. Catcher with a D or F range lets the next pitch get by him for a second passed ball (PB). Runners advance 1 base. Re-roll percentile dice and check batter's PATIENT section to resolve at-bat.
Umpire misses obvious strike; batter walks (BB). Pitcher is rattled, all PATIENT results for this pitcher the remainder of the inning are automatic BB.

Catcher blocks pitch in the dirt. If more than one base runner, the trailing runner takes off while other runners hold. Roll 1d6, if the result is lower or equal to the ARM rating, no throw is made and all runners hold. If the d6 result is higher than the catcher's ARM rating, he throws behind the runner and the runner is tagged out trying to return to his base. The lead runner may attempt to advance by rolling 1d10. If the result is less than his RUN rating, he is safe; otherwise he is thrown out if the d10 result is equal or higher than his RUN rating. Restart the at-bat for this batter.

Catcher with an A range frames the pitch resulting in a SO. Batter is ejected for arguing the call. All other catchers misplay pitch leading to a passed ball (PB). Runners advance 1 base. Batter eventually strikes out, but reaches first on wild pitch with other runners holding and not advancing on the wild pitch.

Pitcher throws a strike that is down the middle, but slightly above the belt. Ump calls the pitch a ball and the batter walks. If the 5th inning or earlier, the pitcher bears down and strikes out the remaining batters this inning. If the 6th inning or later, the pitcher argues the call and is ejected.

rare_plays.name: Rare Plays: Runners On, PATIENT
resolution: Apply the entry below for the re-rolled percentile range.
rare_plays.trigger: Initial percentile 00, pitcher result PATIENT (or PATIENT-OUT or /PATIENT/), runners on base. Re-roll percentile.

chart.result: IF 7th inning or later, strike zone has become increasingly larger each inning. All TOUGH results for both teams are automatic strike outs (SO) for remainder of game. If 6th inning or earlier, all TOUGH results for this pitcher are automatic strike outs (SO) for the remainder of the inning only.

Ump calls obvious strike a ball (BB). Several coaches on pitching team complain about call. Ump does not eject anyone, but squeezes the strike zone even more. Change all TOUGH results to PATIENT for the remainder of the inning while the current pitcher is in the game.

Batter strikes out (SO). Pitcher with a WP range that ends in 32 or higher bounces pitch in dirt. All runners advance 1 base. If 1st base was not occupied or this is the 3rd out of the inning, the batter reaches 1st base and the inning continues. Otherwise, the batter is out.

Batter strikes out (SO) on great pitch by pitcher, but catcher drops the ball. Runners hold. If the 3rd out or 1st base is not occupied, roll 1d6. If equal or less than the catcher's E rating, catcher makes easy throw to 1B to secure the strike out. If the d6 result is higher than the catcher's E rating, catcher throws wildly allowing batter to safely reach base and all runners advance 2 bases. Batter with a RUN rating of 7 or more advances to 2nd base on error; otherwise batter safe at 1st base. Record as SO and E2. Batting team gets an extra out (need 4 outs to complete the inning).

Pitcher with a SO/9 (strike outs per 9 innings) of 6.0 or more causes all batters to roll on their TOUGH sections until a batter reaches base on a hit or the pitcher is removed from the game. Then return to playing as normal. Other pitchers strike out (SO) current batter, but next two batters roll on their WHEELHOUSE section.

Pitcher strikes out remaining batters this inning. If pitcher SO/9 is 5.0 or more, the first three batters he faces next inning roll on their TOUGH sections. All other pitchers, play as normal starting next inning.

Batter strikes out (SO) and ball gets past catcher for passed ball (PB). All runners advance 1 base. If 1st base was not occupied or this is the 3rd out of the inning, the batter reaches 1st base and the inning continues. Otherwise, the batter is out.

Batter strikes out (SO). If the catcher has an A or B range, he catches a low strike and throws out the lead runner trying to advance (if runner on 3rd base, runner is out trying to retreat to 3rd base). Batter is out. All other catchers allow pass ball (PB) and runners advance 1 base. If 1st base was not occupied or this is the 3rd out of the inning, the batter reaches 1st base and the inning continues. Otherwise, the batter is out.

Resolve at-bat using TOUGH section. If batter strikes out, next three batters this pitcher faces roll on their TOUGH section. If batter gets a hit, next three batters this pitcher faces roll on their WHEELHOUSE results. If the batter is out, next three batters pitcher faces roll on their IN-PLAY sections.
Batter strikes out (SO) on awkward swing. Check batter for injury.
Pitcher feels something pop while delivering a pitch, but completes this at-bat eventually walking the batter (BB). Remove pitcher from game and check pitcher for injury.

This batter and all remaining batters this inning roll on their TOUGH section to resolve each at-bat. If both starting pitchers are out of the game, the first batter each inning rolls on WHEELHOUSE and all remaining batters that inning roll on TOUGH for the remainder of the game.

Ump forgets the count and calls ball 4, ball 3. The batter strikes out (SO) on next pitch. Roll 1d6, if the result is 4, the batter argues with the ump about the pitch count and ultimately gets ejected. If the batter is ejected, the first batter for the current pitching team rolls on his TOUGH section next inning.

Pitcher hits batter with pitch, but the ump says the batter swung at the ball and calls the pitch a strike. Roll on the batter's TOUGH section to resolve the at-bat. If the batter strikes out, he has a heated exchange with the umpire, but stays in the game.

rare_plays.name: Rare Plays: Runners On, TOUGH
resolution: Apply the entry below for the re-rolled percentile range.
rare_plays.trigger: Initial percentile 00, pitcher result TOUGH (or TOUGH-OUT), runners on base. Re-roll percentile.

chart.result: If runner on 1st, hard ground ball hits runner. Runner is out; batter safe at 1st on fielder's choice. Other runners advance 1 base. If no runner on 1st base, batter hits a ground ball through the hole into RF. All runners advance 2 bases.

Batter tops ball down 1st base line. Pitcher attempts to field ball near the line and collides with the batter. Umps rule interference on the pitcher and awards batter 1st base; all runners advance 1 base. Give pitcher an error. Check both pitcher and batter for injury.

Batter laces a line drive down the LF line. If the visiting team is batting, the ump rules the ball foul. Re-roll on the batter's IN-PLAY section to complete the at-bat. If the home team is batting, the ump rules the ball fair. Batter is safe on 2nd with a double and all runners score.

Batter smashes a deep fly ball and all runners break for the next base. The CF surprises everyone and makes a running catch. He makes a great throw to double off the lead runner as he tries to return to his base. All others runners return and hold.
Game is momentarily delayed. When it resumes, this batter and all remaining batters this inning roll on their IN-PLAY sections to resolve each at-bat.

If runner on 2nd base, batter hits long single in the gap in right center. All runners advance 2 bases; however, the runner on 2nd appears to have injured his leg running home. Check for injury. If no runner on 2nd base, batter singles and runners advance 2 bases.

Re-roll the 2d6 and check the pitcher's card as normal. All remaining batters this inning automatically check that result until the pitcher is replaced or the inning ends. All runners advance 2 bases on all hits until the inning ends.

Batter lines a single to LF. Lead runner hesitates thinking the ball might be caught and is thrown out at next base. If the runner is forced, change the batter result to a fielder's choice and the runner is forced out trying to advance. Otherwise, the single remains and the runner is tagged out. Other runners advance 1 base and batter stays at 1st base.

Batter hits towering fly ball into short right field. The RF loses the ball in the sun/lights and it drops for a hit with runners advancing 1 base. If the RF has an ARM rating of 7 or less, roll 1d10. If the amount is greater than the batter's RUN rating, he is thrown out before he reaches 1st base by the RF.
Batter lines out into as many outs as possible. If there are two or more runners, the ball is hit to 3B. Otherwise the ball is hit to the SS.
2B dives and catches a sinking line drive. Ump rules the ball was trapped. All runners score while 2B argues with the umpire and batter safe at 1st base with a single.

SS reaches ball grounded up the middle and fires to 1st base. The ball clearly beats the batter, but the ump rules the 1B pulled his foot off the base and batter is safe with a single. All runners score while the 1B argues with the ump.

LF makes sidling attempt on sinking line drive, but catches it on a short hop. If there is a runner on 2nd base, he is thrown out at 3rd base by the LF. If no runner on 2nd base, the runner on 1st base is thrown out at 2nd base by the LF. If no runner on 1st base, the batter is thrown out at 2nd base. Runner on 3rd base (if any) scores and batter is credited with a single. Batter is safe at 1st base if a runner is thrown out.

Batter hits a line drive off the pitcher's glove that is caught by the 1B who doubles off the closest runner. 1B tags runner just off 1st base; otherwise throws to closest base before runner can return.

rare_plays.name: Rare Plays: Runners On, IN-PLAY
resolution: Apply the entry below for the re-rolled percentile range.
rare_plays.trigger: Initial percentile 00, pitcher result IN-PLAY (or /IN-PLAY/), runners on base. Re-roll percentile.

chart.result: Line drive is smashed down the 3rd base line. 3B with an A or B range catches the ball and doubles off closest runner. If there was 2 or more runners and a runner on 1st base, the runner on 1st base is also out for a triple play. 3B with a range of C or worse cannot get to the ball and it bounces into the corner for a double with all runners scoring.

If runner on 1st base, ground ball to SS is fielded and tossed to 2B for the force out. Runner upends 2B and batter is called out due to interference for a double play. Check 2B for injury. If no runner on 1st base, an A or B rated SS throws the batter out. SS with a C or worse range throws late allowing an infield single. In all cases, other runners advance 1 base.

If runner on 1st base, ground ball to 2B is fielded and tossed to SS for the force out. Runner upends SS and batter is called out due to interference for a double play. Check SS for injury. If no runner on 1st base, an A or B rated 2B throws the batter out. 2B with a C or worse range throws late allowing an infield single. In all cases, other runners advance 1 base.
Batter hits a shallow fly ball to CF. Ump rules catcher's interference and awards batter 1st base (score as E2). Runners advance 1 base.
2B fields ball cleanly, but makes a poor throw to 1B. Perform a range check on 1B. If out, score it as a 4-3 out. Otherwise, score as 1 base error on 2B. In all cases, runners advance 1 base.
3B fields ball cleanly, but makes a poor throw to 1B. Perform a range check on 1B. If out, score it as a 5-3 out. Otherwise, score as 1 base error on 3B. In all cases, runners advance 1 base.
Pitcher is called for a balk; all runners advance 1 base. Pitcher is rattled; resolve at-bat using batter's WHEELHOUSE section.
SS fields ball cleanly, but makes a poor throw to 1B. Perform a range check on 1B. If out, score it as a 6-3 out. Otherwise, score as 1 base error on SS. In all cases, runners advance 1 base.

Batter hits a pop fly to LF. Roll 1d6. If equal or less than the LF E rating, ball is caught for the out and the LF fires the ball into the stands. If less than 3 outs, each runner is awarded 1 base and LF is charged with an error. If d6 result is greater than the E rating, LF drops the ball for a 2 base error. All runners score.

Batter hits a pop fly to RF. Roll 1d6. If equal or less than the RF E rating, ball is caught for the out and the RF fires the ball into the stands. If less than 3 outs, each runner is awarded 1 base and RF is charged with an error. If d6 result is greater than the E rating, RF drops the ball for a 2 base error. All runners score.

LF leaps to catch ball at the wall. Resolve as normal Range play. If out, LF catches the ball and all runners advance 1 base. If hit, all runners score and batter is thrown out at 3rd base by the CF trying for a triple. Credit batter with a double.

CF leaps to catch ball at the wall. Resolve as normal Range play. If out, CF catches the ball and all runners advance 1 base. If hit, all runners score and batter is thrown out at 3rd base by the LF trying for a triple. Credit batter with a double.

RF leaps to catch ball at the wall. Resolve as normal Range play. If out, RF catches the ball and all runners advance 1 base. If hit, all runners score and batter is thrown out at 3rd base by the CF trying for a triple. Credit batter with a double.

Catcher attempts to pick off lead runner. Roll 1d6. If greater than the catcher's E rating, the ball sails into the outfield and all runners advance 2 bases. If the d6 is equal or less than the E rating, the throw is on target, but late and the runner is safe. Resolve at-bat using DEFENSE as normal.

A moderate rain begins to fall. It is not enough to postpone play or the game, but makes conditions miserable. Starting with this batter and for the remainder of the game, all DEFENSE checks automatically fail (assume a roll of 01 on the percentile dice). Use DEFENSE to resolve this at-bat.

Amazing job by ground crew has the field in perfect condition. Beginning with this at-bat, all DEFENSE checks for the remainder of the game are automatic outs (assume a roll of 99 on the percentile dice). Use DEFENSE to resolve this at-bat.

Batter legs out an infield single. Perform a range check on 1B. If out, the 1B concealed the ball and tags out the runner when he takes his lead off. If hit, the hidden ball trick does not work and the 1B returns the ball to the pitcher. Resolve the next at-bat using DEFENSE.
If the pitcher has a SO/9 of 4.0 or less, all remaining at-bats this inning use DEFENSE. All other pitchers, resolve this at-bat with DEFENSE and return to play as normal.

Passed ball (PB) by catcher. All runners advance 1 base. Re-roll percentile dice. If result is within pitcher's WP range, charge catcher with a second PB; otherwise re-roll all four dice and check the DEFENSE chart to resolve this at-bat.

rare_plays.name: Rare Plays: Runners On, DEFENSE
resolution: Apply the entry below for the re-rolled percentile range.
rare_plays.trigger: Initial percentile 00, pitcher result DEFENSE (or RANGE or ERROR), runners on base. Re-roll percentile.

rare_plays.name: Balk
resolution: All runners advance 1 base.
On the rare play entry, the pitcher is rattled: resolve the at-bat using the batter's WHEELHOUSE section.
Pick Off chart BALK ranges by Hold rating: Hold 1-3: 96-99; Hold 4-5: 97-99; Hold 6-7: 98-99; Hold 8-9: 99; Hold 10: 99.
rare_plays.trigger: Percentile BALK result on the Pick Off chart (by Hold rating: 96-99, 97-99, 98-99, or 99), or rare play 37-38 on Runners On DEFENSE.

rare_plays.name: Wild Pitch
resolution: All runners advance one base.

Re-roll the percentile dice to resolve the at-bat. If the re-roll is in the WP range again, record a second wild pitch, then use that same roll to resolve the at-bat. If not in the WP range, no wild pitch occurred; all runners hold and the at-bat resolves normally with the same roll.
Pitchers with no WP rating can still throw a wild pitch, but only from the Rare Play charts.

Rare play wild pitch variants: Runners On PATIENT 15-24 (second wild pitch if WP range ends in 33 or higher), 45-54 (wild pitch if WP range ends in 31 or higher; lead runner with RUN 8+ advances 2 bases), 90-94 (batter reaches first on wild pitch after strikeout, other runners hold); Bases Empty PATIENT 84-91 (wild pitch on ball four if WP range ends in 32 or higher; RUN 7+ batter to 3rd, others to 2nd); Runners On TOUGH 23-34 (WP range ending 32+ bounces pitch in dirt, all runners advance 1 base).
rare_plays.trigger: Percentile dice result equals the pitcher's WP rating or falls within his WP range (most pitchers start at 30, e.g. 30-32), with at least one runner on base. Also occurs via rare play entries.

rare_plays.name: Passed Ball
resolution: All runners advance 1 base unless the entry says otherwise.

Rare play sources: Runners On PATIENT 08-14 (catcher with B or worse range misses, PB), 25-34 (C/D/F catcher crossed up, PB), 35-44 (D/F catcher crossed up, PB), 60-69 (passed ball, plus a second PB for D/F catchers), 90-94 (non-A catchers misplay, PB); Runners On TOUGH 60-64 (PB on dropped third strike), 65-69 (non A/B catchers allow PB); Runners On DEFENSE 96-99 (PB, then re-roll: if in pitcher's WP range charge a second PB, else re-roll all four dice on the DEFENSE chart).
A passed ball on a dropped third strike can let the batter reach first (see Dropped Third Strike).
rare_plays.trigger: Catcher fails to handle a pitch, from rare play entries (catcher range checks) or specific play results.

rare_plays.name: Catcher's Interference
resolution: Umpire rules catcher's interference on a shallow fly ball to CF.
Batter is awarded 1st base.
Score as E2.
All runners advance 1 base.
rare_plays.trigger: Rare play entry: Runners On DEFENSE, percentile 22-24.

rare_plays.name: Dropped Third Strike / Wild Pitch Strikeout
resolution: Bases Empty TOUGH 45-64: batter swings at a wild pitch past the catcher; record SO, roll 2d6: equal to or less than batter's RUN rating and the batter beats the throw to 1st (batting team gets an extra out, 4 outs end the inning); greater than RUN and the catcher throws him out to complete the SO.

Bases Empty TOUGH 65-79: catcher drops the third strike; roll 1d6: equal to or less than catcher's E rating and he throws to 1B to secure the SO; higher than E and the throw is wild, batter reaches (RUN 7+ takes 2nd on the error, else 1st). Record as SO and E2; batting team gets an extra out.
Runners On TOUGH 23-34: SO with WP range ending 32+ bouncing in the dirt; all runners advance 1 base; if 1st was unoccupied or it is the 3rd out, the batter reaches 1st and the inning continues.

Runners On TOUGH 35-44: dropped third strike; if 3rd out or 1st unoccupied, roll 1d6 vs catcher's E: clean throw secures the SO, wild throw lets the batter reach and all runners advance 2 bases (RUN 7+ batter to 2nd). Record SO and E2; extra out for the batting team.
Runners On TOUGH 60-64: SO plus passed ball; all runners advance 1 base; batter reaches 1st if 1st was unoccupied or it is the 3rd out.

Runners On TOUGH 65-69: SO; A/B catcher throws out the lead runner trying to advance (or retreating to 3rd); other catchers allow a PB with runners advancing 1 base; batter reaches 1st if 1st was unoccupied or it is the 3rd out.
Runners On PATIENT 90-94: non-A catchers misplay the pitch for a PB; batter strikes out but reaches first on the wild pitch while other runners hold.
rare_plays.trigger: Rare play entries on strikeouts where the catcher fails to secure the ball.

rare_plays.name: Injury Check
resolution: Roll the percentile dice and read the row for the player's injury rating (Prone, Normal, Durable, Iron).

Prone: 0-10 no injury; 11-15 out remainder of game; 16-20 remainder plus 1 game; 21-30 remainder plus 1d6 games; 31-50 remainder plus 10 games; 51-75 remainder plus 20 games; 76-89 remainder plus 50 games; 90-99 out remainder of season.
Normal: 0-30 no injury; 31-50 remainder of game; 51-65 remainder plus 1 game; 66-88 remainder plus 1d6 games; 89-99 remainder plus 10 games.
Durable: 0-69 no injury; 70-84 remainder of game; 85-94 remainder plus 1 game; 95-99 remainder plus 1d6 games.
Iron: 0-69 no injury; 70-89 remainder of game; 90-99 remainder plus 1 game.
'Remainder of game' means the player is removed immediately; additional games missed follow the plus value. '+1d6 games': roll 1d6 for games missed.
Several rare play entries remove the player immediately and specify games missed directly (e.g. pitcher misses next 4 games; batter misses 1d6 games).
rare_plays.trigger: Any play result or rare play entry that says to check a player for injury.

rare_plays.name: Weather Delay
resolution: Bases Empty BALLPARK/WHEELHOUSE 27-56: rain delay (roofed stadium: power outage). Roll 1d6: 1-2 no effect; 3-4 lengthy delay, both pitchers must be replaced; 5-6 game postponed (official if 6th inning or later).

Bases Empty IN-PLAY 12-36: rain delay. 5th inning or later: roll 1d10 after every half inning; if equal to or less than the inning number, umpires call the game (official). Dome or 4th inning or earlier: slight delay, game continues; resolve the at-bat on BALLPARK; WHEELHOUSE result means the next batter checks WHEELHOUSE, IN-PLAY means remaining batters this inning use TOUGH.

Bases Empty IN-PLAY 80-84: dome power outage or violent storm. Roll 2d6 x 10 for delay minutes. 50+ minutes (5+): both pitchers must be replaced. 40 or less (2-4): reduce the pitcher's fatigue rating by 2 and continue.

Runners On BALLPARK/WHEELHOUSE 20-34: rain delay (roofed stadium: power outage). Roll 1d6: 1-2 no effect; 3-4 lengthy delay, both pitchers replaced; 5-6 roll 1d6 after each inning, on a 6 the game is postponed (official if 6th inning or later).
Runners On DEFENSE 71-79: moderate rain for the rest of the game. All DEFENSE checks automatically fail (treat as percentile 01).
Runners On DEFENSE 80-89: perfect field conditions for the rest of the game. All DEFENSE checks are automatic outs (treat as percentile 99).
rare_plays.trigger: Rare play entries for rain or power outages.

rare_plays.name: Ejection
resolution: The ejected player is removed from the game immediately.
Bases Empty PATIENT 06-12: catcher ejected for barking at the umpire (batter walks).
Bases Empty PATIENT 13-24: pitcher ejected for arguing after a walk.
Bases Empty PATIENT 25-30: batter ejected for arguing a called third strike.
Bases Empty PATIENT 31-46: batter HBP; if another HBP occurs this game both benches are warned; any later HBP ejects the pitcher.
Bases Empty PATIENT 47-68: batter charges the mound after HBP; next HBP this game starts a brawl: batter and pitcher ejected and suspended 5 games each.
Bases Empty PATIENT 92-99: batter HBP, benches warned; any further HBP this game ejects the pitcher.
Bases Empty TOUGH 06-12: batter ejected for questioning a called third strike.
Runners On PATIENT 90-94: batter ejected for arguing after an A-range catcher frames a strikeout.
Runners On PATIENT 95-99: 6th inning or later, pitcher ejected for arguing a called ball four.
Runners On TOUGH 90-94: batter ejected for arguing the pitch count (roll of 4 on 1d6); the pitching team's leadoff batter next inning rolls on his TOUGH section.
rare_plays.trigger: Umpire ejects a player, from rare play entries.

rare_plays.name: Pickoff Attempt
resolution: Roll the percentile dice and read the Pick Off chart using the pitcher's Hold rating.
Hold 1-3: WILD? 00-06, CAUGHT 07-34, SAFE 35-95, BALK 96-99.
Hold 4-5: WILD? 00-07, CAUGHT 08-27, SAFE 28-96, BALK 97-99.
Hold 6-7: WILD? 00-08, CAUGHT 09-21, SAFE 22-97, BALK 98-99.
Hold 8-9: WILD? 00-08, CAUGHT 09-16, SAFE 17-98, BALK 99.
Hold 10: WILD? 00-08, CAUGHT 09-12, SAFE 13-98, BALK 99.

WILD?: roll 1d6; equal to or lower than the pitcher's E rating and the throw is on target but late, runner safe. Higher than E and the throw gets past the 1B: re-roll 2d6, if either die is 3 the error goes to the 1B, otherwise to the pitcher. On doubles, all runners advance 2 bases on the error instead of 1.
CAUGHT: runner is out. SAFE: runner is safe. BALK: all runners advance 1 base.
rare_plays.trigger: Double sixes (2d6 = 12) rolled during a stolen base attempt, under any stealing option.

rare_plays.name: Squeeze Play
resolution: Roll all four dice and use the Sacrifice Bunt chart as normal, always using column D.

If the percentile result is in the SH range, the runner may be safe: compare the 2d6 total to the runner's Run rating. Equal to or less than the Run rating and the runner is safe; otherwise he is out (use the LEAD result).
Either way the batter is safe at 1st and all runners advance 1 base.
On a PO result during a suicide squeeze, the runner on 3rd is out: a double play.
rare_plays.trigger: Manager calls a squeeze with a runner on 3rd (never automatic).

rare_plays.name: Optional 0-HR Rule
resolution: Re-roll the percentile dice (00-99).
If the result is doubles (00, 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, 99), the batter hits a home run.
On any other result, check the appropriate Rare Play chart using the 2d6 total currently on the table (or on the previous FAC).
May be ignored if desired.
rare_plays.trigger: Optional. Initial percentile roll is 00 and the batter has a blank or 0 in his WHEELHOUSE HR range.

rare_plays.name: Triple Play
resolution: Line drive smashed down the 3rd base line.
3B with an A or B range catches the ball and doubles off the closest runner.
If there were 2 or more runners including a runner on 1st, the runner on 1st is also out: a triple play.
3B with a C or worse range cannot reach it: double into the corner, all runners score.
rare_plays.trigger: Rare play entry: Runners On DEFENSE, percentile 00-05.

rare_plays.name: Hidden Ball Trick
resolution: Batter legs out an infield single.
Perform a range check on the 1B.
If out, the 1B concealed the ball and tags out the runner when he takes his lead off.
If a hit, the trick fails and the 1B returns the ball to the pitcher.
Resolve the next at-bat using DEFENSE.
rare_plays.trigger: Rare play entry: Runners On DEFENSE, percentile 90-92.
